paper_metadata.title: Approximate complex amplitude encoding algorithm and its application to data classification problems

experiments.description: Training the approximate complex amplitude encoding (ACAE) circuit to load a complex-valued target state for the Iris classification task, using fidelity estimated by classical shadows.

algorithm.variant: Approximate complex amplitude encoding (ACAE) with fidelity-based training
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz with single-qubit Rx/Ry/Rz rotations and CNOT gates

hyperparameters.random_initialization: All rotation axes (X/Y/Z) and parameters initialized randomly

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initialization of rotation axes and angles

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Encode a complex-valued vector into amplitudes of a 5-qubit state; for the Iris example, N=4 features and M=8 training samples, so n=2 data qubits, m=2 index qubits, plus 1 ancilla qubit in the classifier construction
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize fidelity f(θ)=|<Data|ψ(θ)>|^2 between the PQC output state and the target complex-valued data state

problem_instance.description: Iris dataset state-preparation subproblem for later binary classification; training data are the first four samples of Iris setosa and Iris versicolor

dataset_specification.description: Use IDs 1-4 and 51-54 as training data; features are sepal length, sepal width, petal length, petal width; data normalized for amplitude encoding

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare normalized complex target amplitudes from Iris features; classical shadow used to estimate fidelity and gradients
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute fidelity curve and final encoded amplitudes; compare approximate amplitudes to exact data

speedup_claims.factor: O(poly(n)) PQC depth instead of O(2^n) exact state-preparation gates
speedup_claims.baseline_method: exact amplitude encoding / exact state preparation
speedup_claims.conditions: for approximate loading of a complex-valued data vector
speedup_claims.caveats: Classical evaluation of the fidelity estimate still includes an O(2^n) summation over amplitudes; the quantum advantage is in circuit depth, not overall end-to-end runtime.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: PQC depth O(l n) with l = O(1) to O(poly(n)); data encoding target requires O(2^n) amplitudes
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical evaluation of fidelity estimate includes O(2^n) summation over amplitudes; exact state preparation generally requires O(2^n) gates

experiments.description: Applying ACAE to implement the compact Hadamard classifier for Iris binary classification, including both training-data encoding and test-data encoding circuits.

algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz for training-data encoding; 2-qubit ansatz with only Ry gates and CNOT gates for test-data encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Training-data encoder: 400 iterations; test-data encoder: 100 iterations

hyperparameters.balanced_classes_assumption: M+ = M- = M/2 for the main derivation; imbalanced case handled by tuning ϕ

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Random initialization of all rotation axes and angles for the training encoder; test encoder initialized as a small Ry/CNOT ansatz

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Compact amplitude encoding stores two real vectors in real and imaginary parts of one quantum state; CHC uses ancilla A, index register J, and data register D. For Iris, N=4 and M=8, so n=2, m=2, total qubits = 5
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification via sign of <σz(A)> = sgn[1/2 Σ_j b'_j y_j <x̃|x_j>]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Uniform weights bj = 2/M; relative phase ϕ chosen as π/4 for balanced classes, or tan(ϕ)=M-/M+ for imbalanced classes

problem_instance.description: Binary classification on Iris dataset: Iris setosa vs Iris versicolor, and separately Iris versicolor vs Iris virginica

dataset_specification.description: Training: IDs 1-4 and 51-54 for setosa-versicolor task; test: IDs 5-8 and 55-58. For versicolor-virginica task, analogous IDs 55-58 and 105-108 are used. Features: sepal length, sepal width, petal length, petal width

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Encode training and test vectors into complex amplitudes; train U(θ) offline on all training data and U'(θ') online for each test datum; use classical shadows for fidelity estimation
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla Z expectation and take its sign as the predicted label

speedup_claims.factor: fewer gates than original CHC; avoids exponentially many gates for exact initial-state preparation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: original compact Hadamard classifier with exact compact amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.conditions: when using ACAE to approximate the training and test encoders
speedup_claims.caveats: No direct runtime or wall-clock comparison is reported; the claim is about gate complexity.

experiments.description: Applying ACAE-assisted CHC to credit card fraud detection using a public Kaggle dataset with four selected features and a small training subset.

algorithm.variant: ACAE-assisted compact Hadamard classifier (CHC) for fraud detection
algorithm.ansatz: hardware-efficient ansatz for training-data encoding; small Ry/CNOT ansatz for test-data encoding
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Not explicitly stated for the fraud experiment; same ACAE training procedure as the Iris demonstration

hyperparameters.phase_parameter: ϕ chosen as in CHC construction; exact value not explicitly stated for this experiment

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not explicitly stated; same random initialization strategy as ACAE training

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Use 4 features from the 28 PCA-transformed features of each transaction; encode normal and fraudulent training data into real and imaginary parts of a complex amplitude, respectively
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of a transaction as normal (+1) or fraudulent (-1) using the sign of the ancilla expectation value
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Uniform weighting over training samples; CHC sign rule

problem_instance.description: Credit card fraud detection on Kaggle creditcardfraud dataset

dataset_specification.description: European cardholder transactions from September 2013; 284,807 transactions total with 492 fraudulent transactions; features include Time, Amount, and 28 PCA-transformed variables, of which V1-V4 are used here; training uses 4 normal and 4 fraudulent samples

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Select 4 normal and 4 fraudulent training samples; use V1-V4 features; normalize data for amplitude encoding; train ACAE encoders and then classify test transactions
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla Z expectation and classify by sign; additional simulation on 48 randomly selected instances reported 42/48 correct

speedup_claims.factor: fewer gates than original CHC; avoids exponentially many gates for exact initial-state preparation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: original compact Hadamard classifier with exact compact amplitude encoding
speedup_claims.conditions: for the ACAE-assisted fraud detection circuit
speedup_claims.caveats: No classical baseline model or runtime comparison is reported; the paper only reports classification outcomes.

experiments.description: Scalability study of ACAE on the credit card fraud detection setting, varying the number of data points/qubits and measuring circuit depth needed to reach target fidelities.

algorithm.ansatz: variational quantum circuit (same general ACAE hardware-efficient style)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Depth required to reach fidelity thresholds 0.90, 0.95, or 0.99

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same credit-card-fraud-style encoding, but with varying dataset sizes; number of qubits scales with the number of data points
problem_formulation.objective_function: Reach a target fidelity between model and target states

problem_instance.description: Scaling analysis on the same credit card fraud detection problem, with dataset sizes from 64 to 1024 data points

dataset_specification.description: Same Kaggle dataset; study varies number of data points and corresponding qubits, with reported cases from 64 (5 qubits) to 1024 (9 qubits)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Run numerical simulations for multiple dataset sizes and record circuit depth needed to achieve each fidelity threshold
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Plot depth versus number of qubits; observe superlinear growth

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports only that required depth increases superlinearly with qubit count; no explicit speedup over classical methods is claimed.
